devices.ATIforcesensors: Connects to the ATI force sensors server
devices.DAQ: This client connects to a DAQ server to sample one or more channels (e.g. for a button box or force sensors).
devices.NIDAQ: This client connects to a NIDAQ server to sample one or more channels (e.g. for a button box or force sensors).
devices.arduino: This client connects to an arduino server to sample one or more digital channels
devices.bluetera: Connect to a bluetera server to record orientation + acceleration data
devices.character: This is a client to connect to a character server (over TCP/IP)
devices.fastrak: Connect to a fastrak server to record fastrak 6D data
devices.fixedglove: Use fixed joint angles in place of a glove.
devices.fixedtracker: Use a fixed position / orientation in place of a tracker.
devices.forcesensors: This client connects to a DAQ server to sample force sensors.
devices.g4: Connect to the g4 to sample from it
devices.gazepoint: Connect to the gaze point server to sample from the eye tracker
devices.glove: Connect to the cyberglove server to collect glove data
devices.gloveemulator: Read glove data from a file. The files should be in the directory "emulated" and the name of the file to read is specified in each trial in the filename field.
devices.glovetracker: This connects to both a glove and tracker (fastrak / liberty) server (or emulator).
devices.gopro: A client to connect to a GoPro camera to record video
devices.keyboard: Connect to a keyboard server to record keystroke information
devices.liberty: Connect to the liberty to sample from it
devices.mouse: Connect to the mouse server to sample the mouse location
devices.optotrak: Connects to the optotrak to sample 3D locations
devices.redamber: Connect to a redamber server to record orientation + acceleration data
devices.serialport: Connect to a serial port and sample from it
devices.tablet: Connects to server to sample location and other information from a WACOM tablet
devices.trackeremulator: Read tracker data from a file. The files should be in the directory "emulated" and the name of the file to read is specified in each trial in the filename field.
devices.trakStar: Connect to a trakStar server to record trakStar 6D data
devices.video: A client to connect to a program to record video

stimulus.circle: A circle to be drawn in each frame
stimulus.dots: A dot to be drawn in each frame
stimulus.fingerOppositionSequence: Provide feedback when using finger opposition sequence target
stimulus.fixation: Displays a fixation point in the center of the screen
stimulus.images: Display images (from those specified in the images section in setup), optionally with noise
stimulus.line: A line to be drawn in each frame
stimulus.none: This is for when no stimulus is required. It does nothing.
stimulus.rectangle: A rectangle to be drawn in each frame
stimulus.showImage: Show a single image for the whole trial
stimulus.showText: Show a string of text for the whole trial
stimulus.symbols: Present some symbols (i.e. arbitrary text) at specified times
stimulus.textArray: Draw an array (rows x columns) of a character at the specified positions

targetType.buttonPress: The response is pressing a button, using a button box connected to a DAQ card
targetType.colorInImage: The target(s) are defined by a color in an image
targetType.defineTarget: This response is to define a target for use later (e.g. with the response targetInSpace).
targetType.dummy: The dummy response does not record any response
targetType.fingerOppositionSequence: The response is touching the thumb and another finger in a sequence N times
targetType.imageState: The target is a state (using images stimuli)
targetType.keyboard: This response is pressing a key on the keyboard
targetType.keyboardsequence: The response is pressing a certain sequence of keys N times
targetType.mouseEntersBox: The response is moving the mouse into one of the specified boxes (which can be invisible)
targetType.movementThreshold: This response is moving past a certain location
targetType.pointToPoint: This response is for (possibly repeated) point to point measurements.
targetType.showdata: This response does not stop the trial, but shows feedback (similar to showPosition).
targetType.stoppedMoving: This response is to stop a trial after the subject has stopped moving for a certain amount of time.
targetType.targetInSpace: The target(s) are locations in space
targetType.targetOnScreen: Response of touching a target (e.g. on a touchscreen)
targetType.trigger: The trial ends when an external trigger is received

starttrial.button: The trial starts when a button is pressed, using a button box connected to a DAQ card. To use this, setup.MCtrigger should be set to 1 (for input), or there should be a DAQ device defined as a response device
starttrial.colorInImage: The start position are defined by a color in an image
starttrial.keyboard: The trial is started by pressing a key
starttrial.mouseClick: The trial starts when the mouse button is clicked, optionally in a (possibly invisible) box
starttrial.mouseInBox: The trial starts when the mouse enters (or is already in) a (potentially invisible) box
starttrial.pedal: Start the trial by pressing a pedal
starttrial.stylusButton: Start the trial when the tablet stylus button is pressed
starttrial.targetInSpace: The target(s) are locations in space
starttrial.trigger: The trial starts when an external trigger is received

ATIforcesensors.name: server
ATIforcesensors.description: Location of the server (e.g. 'localhost' or an IP address)

ATIforcesensors.name: port
ATIforcesensors.description: Port to connect to the server on

ATIforcesensors.name: showPositionType
ATIforcesensors.description: If showing position, how to show the current position (either 'dot','line','ellipse', 'rectangle' or 'image' or the name of a function with an @ before it). Line means a line from the last point to the current point. Note that if showPosition=1, it will always be shown. If showPosition=2 and imagestimulus is used,it will only be shown when in state 1. If showPosition=3, then the fields below will be used to determine the position. If showPosition=4, it is the same as 3, but the position is only shown until the trial starts. If showPosition=5, it is the same as 3, but if using image stimuli, only show position if it is in state 1.If using a function, the function will get called every frame (data can be stored between calls in the thistrial struct): thistrial = yourFunctionName(experimentdata,thistrial,lastpositionVisual,e,frame);

ATIforcesensors.name: showPositionColor
ATIforcesensors.description: If showing position, the color of the feedback (each number between 0 and 255). Should be a N * (P*3) array (P= number of dots). Can either have one row, or a row for each frame. If showing image, the imagenumber to show. If it is a cell array, then each cell can specify for an individual trial.

ATIforcesensors.name: showPositionSize
ATIforcesensors.description: If showing position and showPositionType is a dot, then a 1*P array (with the size of the each dot in pixels. If type is a rectangle, then a 1*(P*2) array (width and height).

ATIforcesensors.name: showPositionRotationCenter
ATIforcesensors.description: If showing position, the center of rotation (if showPositionRotationAngle is not zero). Should be a P * 2 matrix (p = number of dots), in relative screen coordinates (i.e. between 0 and 1)

ATIforcesensors.name: showPositionRotationAngle
ATIforcesensors.description: If showing position, the angle to rotate about the center of rotation (in radians). Should be a P * 1 matrix (p = number of dots), or a cell for each trial with a P*1 matrix

ATIforcesensors.name: startRotationFrame
ATIforcesensors.description: If showing position, the frame to start the rotation (if there is one). To start before the trial (i.e. while waiting for start), set to -inf. Should be a 1*P  matrix (p=number of dots) or N*P (one row for each trial).

ATIforcesensors.name: displayRangeX
ATIforcesensors.description: Range of values to show when using showPosition=3 as the dot position on the x axis. The ith row corresponds to the ith sensor. Use the first two values to show the x values, next two for y. e.g. [-1 1 0 0 0] to show x values of -1 to 1 as the dot x position. Use the last value to show time, e.g. [0 0 0 0 1] will move across the screen in 1 s. If the time (last) value is set to -inf, only show before trial starts. If set to inf, only show during (and not before) trial. This should be a cell array with either a single cell for all trials, or a cell for each trial. To show multiple points, use an M*(N*P) matrix (M sensors, N=2*dims+1, P dots)

ATIforcesensors.name: displayRangeY
ATIforcesensors.description: Range of values to show when using showPosition=3 as the dot position on the y axis. The ith row corresponds to the ith sensor. Use the first two values to show the x values, next two for y, e.g. [0 0 -10 10 0] to show y values of -0.5 to 0.5 as the dot y position. Use the last value to show time, e.g. [0 0 0 0 1] will move up the screen in 1 s. If the time (last) value is set to -inf, only show before trial starts. If set to inf, only show during (and not before) trial. This should be a cell array with either a single cell for all trials, or a cell for each trial. To show multiple points, use an M*(N*P) matrix (M sensors, N=2*dims+1, P dots)

ATIforcesensors.name: offsetX
ATIforcesensors.description: x offset when using showPosition.  This can either be a 1*P matrix [P is the number of dots] (same for every trial), or an NxP matrix (one row for each trial).

ATIforcesensors.name: offsetY
ATIforcesensors.description: y offset when using showPosition.  This can either be a 1*P matrix [P is the number of dots] (same for every trial), or an NxP matrix (one row for each trial).

QUEST.description: threshold criterion (midpoint of table will yield this threshold)

QUEST.name: delta
QUEST.description: delta parameter of Weibull function (fraction of trials the observer presses blindly)

QUEST.name: gamma
QUEST.description: gamma parameter of Weibull function (fraction of trials that will generate response 1 when stimulus intensity = -inf)

QUEST.name: min
QUEST.description: minimum value to show - the value shown will always be >= to this value, regardless of what Quest suggests

QUEST.name: max
QUEST.description: maximum value to show - the value shown will always be <= to this value, regardless of what Quest suggests
